questions.prompt: A plant's machine log records the diameter of **every** one of the 52 000 shafts it made last month; their mean is 25.013 mm. Quality control also measured 40 of those shafts by hand and got a mean of 25.009 mm. Which number is a parameter?
options: 25.013 mm, because it describes all 52 000 shafts made last month
25.009 mm, because it was measured by hand and is more careful
Both of them, because both describe shafts made by the same plant
Neither of them, because a parameter can never be calculated
questions.explanation: A parameter describes the whole population. The log covers every shaft, so its mean, 25.013 mm, is μ. The 40 hand-measured shafts are a sample, so 25.009 mm is a statistic, x̄, however carefully it was measured. A parameter is usually unknown, but here the population was measured in full.

questions.prompt: Match each symbol with what it stands for.
questions.explanation: Greek letters (μ, σ, and p for a proportion) are parameters of the population. Latin letters and hats (x̄, s, p̂) are statistics calculated from a sample.

questions.prompt: Anchor bolts from a supplier have a mean pull-out strength of μ = 250 kN, from the supplier's records of all its production. A contractor tests 12 of them and gets x̄ = 253.4 kN. What is the sampling error x̄ − μ, in kN? Give it to one decimal, with its sign.
questions.explanation: Sampling error = x̄ − μ = 253.4 − 250 = +3.4 kN. The sample came out a little high, by chance: which 12 bolts happened to be tested.

questions.prompt: Which of these changes from one random sample to the next, when the samples come from the same population?
options: The sample mean x̄ of the measurements in each sample
The population mean μ of all the items being sampled
The population standard deviation σ of all the items
The number N of items in the population being sampled
questions.explanation: μ, σ and N describe the population, which stays the same. Each new sample has different members, so its mean x̄ is different. That variation is what the sampling distribution describes.

questions.prompt: An engineer samples 50 welds and finds a mean strength 6 MPa below the plant's long-run mean μ. The gauge was calibrated that morning and the welds were picked at random. What is the most likely cause of the 6 MPa difference?
options: Sampling error: chance in which 50 welds were picked
Bias from the gauge, which must be read too low
A mistake in the calculation of the sample mean
A change in the population mean μ since the records
questions.explanation: A random sample from a calibrated gauge still misses μ by chance: that is sampling error, and it is expected. Whether 6 MPa is more than chance would explain is a question for the sampling distribution (item 6.5) and for the tests of Module 8. Nothing in the question points to bias, an arithmetic slip, or a change in μ.
